topics: 1.1. Introduction to Thermodynamics  Definition and scope of thermodynamics  Importance and applications in engineering.

1.2. Basic Concepts and Definitions  System, surroundings and universe  Types of systems (closed, open, isolated)  Properties of a system (extensive and intensive)  State, state functions, and process  Equilibrium, types of equilibrium
1.3. Energy and the First Law of Thermodynamics  Work and heat  The first law of thermodynamics (energy conservation)  Internal energy, enthalpy, and specific heats
1.4. Second Law of Thermodynamics  Introduction to entropy  Reversible and irreversible processes  The second law of thermodynamics  Heat engines, refrigerators, and heat pumps.
1.5. Represent constant pressure, constant volume, constant temperature, adiabatic and polytrophic process on P-V and T-S diagram.
1.6. Ideal gas and their basic laws.

1.7. Introduction to modes of heat transfer and types of work. units.title: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics
topics: 2.1. Introduction to Fluid Mechanics  Definition and scope of fluid mechanics  Importance and applications in engineering.  Properties of fluids (density, viscosity, surface tension, specific volume, thermal conductivity, specific heat capacity, compressibility.)
2.2. Fluid statics  Pressure and its measurement (Concept of atmospheric pressure, gauge pressure, vacuum, absolute pressure and pressure measuring devices.)  Pascal’s law

2.3. Fluid kinematics and Dynamics  Types of fluid flow- Steady, unsteady, laminar, turbulent-, one-, two- and three-dimensional flow, uniform and non-uniform flow.  Continuity equation.  Bernoulli’s theorem  Flow rate measurement (orifice, Venturi, and Pitot tube)
2.4. Introduction to Pneumatics  Definition and scope of Pneumatics.  Importance and application of Pneumatics.
uos: 2.a. Recognize importance of fluid mechanics and define various properties of fluid.
2.b. Comprehend concept of pressure and its measurement.
2.d. Explain the types of fluid flow.
2.e. Explain continuity equation and Bernoulli’s theorem.
2.f. Explain flow rate measurement with orifice, venture and Pitot tube.
2.g. Explain importance and application of Pneumatics.
